failureClassifications.description: All six canonical-v1 Death Knight first attempts violated the explicit eight-percent safe-margin gate despite complete silhouettes.
failureClassifications.resolution: Added the versioned safe-frame-v2 prompt protocol for ungenerated targets while preserving every completed pilot prompt hash. The first safe-frame-v2 Elemental passed framing without a retry.

failureClassifications.description: Independent known-target audit found unstable command-seal and pennant grammar plus repeated base-armor-and-overlay affinity treatment; Metal was especially difficult to distinguish from Normal.

Independent audit found that the Stone Breaker anchor biased every Bound Vanguard toward a raised head-like crown and stone substrate; Normal reads Earth, Water reads Ice, and Fire, Metal, and Wind often read as stone plus effects.
failureClassifications.resolution: Create a purpose-built headless, materially neutral Bound Vanguard anchor and versioned Elemental regression targets with affinity-specific load-bearing substance rules.

failureClassifications.description: The basic-v1 authoring contract required framing and subject completion but allowed visually polished semantic failures to remain producer candidates.
failureClassifications.resolution: Added semantic-v2 gates for manifest fidelity, real multi-dimensional affinity construction or unaffiliated Normal construction, and a visibly readable counterplay cue. Completed pilot targets retain basic-v1 for immutable provenance.

failureClassifications.description: The first Grey Wolf Normal generation returned no bindable image payload and consumed the sole retry.
failureClassifications.resolution: The second call returned a verifiable candidate; retain the provider-failure attempt as evidence and do not generalize a new visual rule from one empty response.

failureClassifications.description: A fresh-agent audit found that safe-frame-v3 removed the terminal newline but accidentally omitted the documented central-84-percent framing lock, contributing to framing-only retries in the beast wave.
failureClassifications.resolution: Preserved all dispatched v3 prompts as immutable provenance and introduced safe-frame-v4, which restores the central-canvas lock while retaining the no-terminal-LF handoff. Metal and Water Cave Bears passed v4 framing on their first attempts.

failureClassifications.description: The verifier conflated manifest reference provenance with the generated-image source used for a corrective edit, making a truthful correction record fail validation.
failureClassifications.resolution: Defined ordered referenceInputs as inherited target provenance and correctionReferenceInput as the exact generated-image edit source path and hash; updated both contract and verifier, then verified the truthful Wood Bear revise result.

failureClassifications.description: Local configuration requests 16 concurrent threads, but this live task exposes four total slots and therefore only three simultaneous image workers when orchestration is reserved.
failureClassifications.resolution: Use three image workers as the safe ceiling in this environment. Run 8-, 12-, and 16-worker stages only in a newly provisioned task that exposes those slots; do not infer capacity from configuration alone.

completionNotes: Canary metrics cover Normal and Fire Death Knights at two effective workers. The partial Pilot covers Wood, Metal, and Water Death Knights at three effective workers under a four-job planned stage; the active task exposes four total slots and reserves one for orchestration.

Queue delay is unknown because dispatch and provider-queue timestamps are not separately recorded. Effective speedup is the observed summed-job-time to wave-wall-time ratio, not a causal serial-control benchmark.
P90 and P95 remain null at these sample sizes. Candidate rates are producer-authoring outcomes; blind human recognition and approval remain pending.
Rejected intermediate images retain prompt, source identifier, timing, and findings but not byte-level persistence receipts; complete provenance currently refers to selected retained candidates.

Safe-frame-v2 produced first-attempt framing passes for five of six Elementals; Fire still required one correction for a top-edge flame wake and head-like chassis. Grey Wolf Normal used its retry for an empty provider response rather than framing.

The six-target semantic Elemental regression ran at three effective workers in two scheduler waves: five producer candidates, one revise, full provenance, no throttle, timeout, collision, or integration error. The final v4 Bear wave produced two first-attempt candidates and one bounded revise with the same workflow integrity.

The controlled matrix is complete at 21 producer candidates and 3 revise results, but only 10 of 24 were first-attempt candidates versus the plan threshold of 20. Human blind species/affinity recognition is still zero because no human review has been recorded, so the breadth release gate remains closed.
